newsitem.title: USA: Swiss banks said to support Holocaust disclosure.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks said to support Holocaust disclosure.

text.p: The Swiss Banking Association has declared support for public disclosure of the bank accounts of Second World War Holocaust victims to locate their heirs, Senator Al D'Amato said on Wednesday.

"It's about time," the Senate Banking Committee chairman told the Senate. "They've held these names secretly for 52 years. Now finally they're taking this most basic step towards finding the rightful heirs."
Jewish groups claim Swiss banks may be silently holding billions of dollars in wealth left by Hitler's victims.

D'Amato, a New York Republican, released a letter from the Swiss Banking Association supporting public disclosure of the accounts but saying a mechanism must be found to do it consistent with Swiss law and sound banking practices.
The letter said Credit Suisse Group, Union Bank of Switzerland and Swiss Bank Corp. have pledged to share costs of publicising the names worldwide when the mechanism is found.

"I am writing to express the SBA's unequivocal support for the concept of public disclosure of the names of account holders in the very special and limited circumstances presented by Holocaust-related dormant assets," an SBA official said in the letter to the Swiss Federal Banking Commission.
"It is our hope that ... a mechanism will be implemented soon that will permit such disclosure consistent with Swiss law and sound banking practices."
"When such a mechanism is put in place, the names of account holders can be disseminated throughout the world."
